A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same work, renamed from GWRF to GRaF, with matching authors, core architecture and retained experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable in both versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RFID and MATLAB spectrum-synthesis experiments, component ablations, interpolation analyses and an angle-of-arrival case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations on new layouts, simulation-to-real transfer, fine-tuning, cross-frequency transfer and neighbor-count sensitivity.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 specifies complex signal/attenuation MLP outputs and propagation-weighted aggregation in Equations 14–15. However, Appendix D repeats v1's ten-head Transformer, mean pooling and amplitude-output procedure. The PDFs do not resolve whether the new formulation changes inference or interprets the existing implementation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates RFID data and conference/office simulations. v2 adds bedroom and outdoor environments, simulation-to-real RFID transfer, and testing across frequency bands without retraining. These substantially broaden environmental coverage and distribution-shift scenarios.

E2.justification: KNN, KNN-DL and NeRF2 remain the comparators in corresponding main experiments. The added transfer experiments reuse KNN-DL and NeRF2. Newly discussed RFScape, GeRaF and Gaussian-splatting approaches are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces fixed-voxel cross-frequency testing, RFID fine-tuning using 20% of its training data, and frozen-model neighbor-count sweeps with radius 10 wavelengths. Appendix D also states target-scene fine-tuning for NeRF2, unlike v1's stated source-scene training protocol; it does not establish whether retained scores were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component ablations and AoA study remain. v2 adds neighbor-count sensitivity, cross-frequency failure analysis, simulation-to-real performance before and after fine-tuning, and an end-to-end computational-cost analysis. These test substantial additional questions about robustness, adaptation and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the interpolation experiment's mean PSNR of 20.5 dB, standard deviation of 4.1 dB and CDF summaries. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Its Gaussian likelihood assumption belongs to the theoretical loss derivation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical scores. v2 adds substantial results, including bedroom/outdoor PSNRs of 9.43/6.83 dB and RFID transfer PSNRs of 4.54 without and 15.97 with fine-tuning. Reported model size changes from 27.1 to 478.6 MB and inference time from 1.79 to 1.95 seconds in the overhead table.

T1.justification: v1 supports interpolation empirically. v2 adds Theorem 1 and Appendix A.1's quadratic error bound under smoothness and convex-hull assumptions, an electromagnetic derivation of ray aggregation in Appendix B, and a deterministic-latent Gaussian-likelihood derivation of the existing L2 objective in Appendix C.

C1.justification: v2 promotes a proved RF interpolation theorem and its error guarantee to a central contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion; v1 presents interpolation as an empirical observation. The principal claims of neighboring-spectrum synthesis and cross-scene generalization remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussions: the bound concerns linear interpolation, cross-frequency failure reflects propagation and resolution differences, severe layout shifts may require adaptation, temporal dynamics are unmodeled, and deployment requires neighboring measurements. It also adds simulation rationale and computational tradeoffs beyond v1's shorter cross-layout caveat.

D1.justification: Most training and architecture settings are retained. v2 newly documents wavelength-based voxel sizing, new-scene dimensions and sample counts, and simulation costs. Conversely, v1's explicit geometry-attention formula and promised future code release disappear. Neither PDF supplies a code-access location.

R1.justification: Section 3 substantially expands positioning to include RFScape, GeRaF and several RF Gaussian-splatting approaches, distinguishing cross-scene synthesis from geometry reconstruction and single-scene acceleration. Additional optical NeRF and propagation-theory references broaden the research context.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming GWRF to GRaF, v2 extensively rewrites the introduction and methodology around interpolation theory and latent variables. Implementation material moves to Appendix D, supplementary sections are reorganized, and the earlier impact statement and acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: v2 adds an opening overview figure and new-layout visualizations, expands Figure 6 from four to seven spectrum examples, and adds several experimental tables. Earlier interpolation figures are merged, the ray-tracing diagram moves into the appendix, and the document's typography and visual organization change substantially.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's conference/office generalization tests, v2's broader transfer experiments, sensitivity analysis and explicit limitations better establish where the approach works and fails. However, unresolved agreement between the ray-tracing equations and Appendix D, unclear NeRF2 fine-tuning for retained results, and runtime accounting that still uses 1.79 seconds despite Table 12 reporting 1.95 seconds limit the overall gain.
